Notation 1. Given a group (G, f) and g1, g2 ∈G, we will use the notation
g1 · g2 := f(g1, g2).
In particular, condition (A) translates into
g1 · (g2 · g3) = (g1 · g2) · g3.
Moreover, we will denote the identity element by 1.

We can also construct a group ⟨a⟩= {g ∈G : g = an, n ∈Z}, the group of elements of G generated by a. Using Lagrange’s theorem, we can show
|a| | |G|

$| a | | | G |$
since $\langle a \rangle$ is a subgroup of $G$ and so $| \langle a \rangle | | | G |$, and $| \langle a \rangle | = | a |$ (exercise).
